note: The descent from Gologorica to Brisbane. Generations 1-4 rest on two Status Animarum entries and one baptismal entry from the Gracisce parish books, certified by the Pazin State Archive in 2021. Generations 5-6 rest on wartime and displaced-persons paper held by the Arolsen Archives. The last two generations are given as the family itself publishes them, without dates.

generations.name: Giovanni Defranceschi
generations.evidence: Carried on the family's own descent chart. The Status Animarum entry for his son calls that son Joan. Bapt. Defranceschi, and the next generation is styled q. Joannis — son of the late Giovanni — so a Giovanni stands at the head of the line. The 1750–1829 dates come from the family chart, not yet from a register page. What is no longer in doubt is the place: the Klenovica register of 1890 records Gallignana as this family's zavičaj, its inherited commune, four generations downstream.

generations.name: Giovanni Battista Defranceschi
generations.evidence: Status Animarum of the parish of Gallignana, house 5. Name, condition, birth, marriage and death in the ruled columns; wife and four sons beneath him.

generations.name: Josip Defranceschi
generations.evidence: Baptised at Gallignana on 23 March 1863, born the day before, son of Antonius the stonecutter. He is the generation that leaves Istria for the Kvarner coast: his son is born at Crikvenica in 1890. The family identifies his wife as Anna Kalanj, and her own baptism survives — Ledenice register, entry 2 of 1864, daughter of Josephus Kalanj and Rosalia née Perković, at Rijenovica house 22, in the Vinodol valley directly above Crikvenica. That is very probably the reason a Gračišće stonecutter's son ended up on that stretch of coast: he married into it. The 1951 death date is the family's.

spouse.name: Anna Kalanj
spouse.born: 3 January 1864, at Rijenovica in the Vinodol

generations.flag: The marriage itself has still not been found — only its consequences. The 1890 baptism names Josip and Ana as husband and wife, which settles that they married; the page and year of the wedding would say when the family reached the coast, and is the next thing to ask Rijeka or Pazin for.

generations.name: Anton Rudolf Defranceski
generations.evidence: Entry 9 of the Klenovica baptisms for 1890: Anton Rudolf, legitimate, son of «Josip Defranceschi i žena Ana Kalanj rodjena», at house 22 — and in the column for the parents' place of origin, «Gallignana u Istriji». That is the zavičaj, the inherited Austrian commune of legal settlement, and it is the register itself stating that this coastal household's home commune was Gračišće. Fifty-seven years later he is on the Pfullingen list of foreigners, and a certificate of 1950 gives his birth as 20 January 1890 at Crikvenica — the same day, the same man, the coastal parish named by its market town rather than its village.
generations.flag: The mayor's certificate is dated seven years after the death year the family carries. Retrospective certificates of this kind were commonly obtained by a surviving son for a pension or restitution claim, but the point is open.
